newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK says no decision on intervening property market.
newsitem.headline: HK says no decision on intervening property market.

text.p: Hong Kong government has not decided on when and how to curb speculation in the real estate market, Secretary for Housing Dominic Wong said on Monday.

"There is no clear time for us to take such a decision," Wong told reporters. "I'll monitor the situation very carefully and if necessary, we'll announce measures in order to deal with the situation."
"I think prices are generally reasonble and have been developing in a steady and healthy manner," he said.
"But there have been speculative activities particularly in respect of luxury flats. That has been giving the Hong Kong government great concern," he added.

He said the administration was taking a closer look at speculative activities in the luxury property sector, and was studying ways to increase land supply, such as speeding up procedures for releasing land.
Wong was speaking after meeting Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa who will govern the territory after Britain hands the colony back to China on July 1.
The housing official said he would from time to time discuss housing policy with Tung, who told a luncheon on Monday that the long-term solution to high property prices was to increase land supply.
Tung reiterated that he was not in favour of using administrative measures to intervene in the property market.

A growing wave of speculation in the luxury property sector has recently sparked fears of possible government intervention in the property market, and the concern dragged down local property stocks on Monday.
